original_interpretation: Interpretation: the May 2025 EDA restriction came via individual 'is-informed' letters, not a published rule, explaining differing dates (Cadence letter 23 May; Synopsys letter received 29 May) and no Federal Register citation.
evidence_found: Cadence 8-K: "on May 23, 2025, the Bureau of Industry and Security ('BIS') ... informed Cadence ... that a license was required"; Synopsys 8-K: "pursuant to a letter received on May 29, 2025"; Kirkland: "The outreach appears to take the form of a traditional BIS 'is informed' letter"; Federal Register API (BIS, 'electronic design automation', May-Aug 2025): count 0

original_interpretation: Interpretation: DLA Piper says Cadence admitted 61 EAR violations; the BIS press release cites 56 + 2.
evidence_found: BIS order: "...Proposed Charging Letter ... alleges that Respondent committed 61 violations"; Charges 1-56 CSCC, 57-58 Phytium, 59-61 downloads by Mikron, Huawei, SMIC. BIS press release: "Cadence admitted to 56 violations" ... "two more violations". DLA Piper: "Cadence also admitted to 61 violations of the EAR"
correction: Both statements are accurate, and the gap is now explained: the BIS order lists 61 charges, the press release omits the 3 Entity-List download charges (Mikron, Huawei, SMIC, Sept 2016-Dec 2021). The 'unresolved' note no longer applies; CON-0050 updated to resolved.
notes: New claim from the BIS order added; CON-0050 set to resolved/comparable=false with the new claim as more defensible.

original_interpretation: Inference: open PDKs posted on GitHub under Apache 2.0 are likely 'published' under 734.7 and outside the EAR; leading-edge NDA-only commercial PDKs are not published and remain subject to export controls and deemed-export rules.
evidence_found: 734.7(a)(4): published includes "posting on the Internet on sites available to the public" without dissemination restrictions. 734.3(a): subject to the EAR are "(1) All items in the United States ... (2) All U.S. origin items wherever located; (3) Foreign-made ... technology that is commingled with controlled U.S.-origin technology"
correction: First half follows from 734.7 (open PDKs are publicly posted under Apache 2.0 with no dissemination limits). Second half overreaches: an NDA-only PDK is not 'published', but whether it is subject to the EAR depends on 734.3. A foreign foundry's PDK (e.g. TSMC, Samsung) is foreign-origin technology, subject to the EAR only when in the US, or when commingled with US-origin controlled content or under foreign direct product rules. The foundry's home-country export controls may also apply.
notes: Not a legal opinion; BIS has not ruled publicly on PDKs.

original_interpretation: Inference: four quarters of ESD Alliance data (~US$5.5-5.7bn/quarter) imply ~US$21-23bn annual EDA+IP+services, broadly consistent with Synopsys's US$22.5bn 2025.
evidence_found: ESD releases: Q2 2025 "$5,089.4 million"; Q3 2025 "$5,566.4 million"; Q4 2025 "$5,466.3 million"; Q1 2026 release gives Q1 2025 as "$5,098.3 million" (Q1 2026 "$5,747.8 million"). CY2025 sum = US$21.2bn vs Synopsys "EDA & IP $22.5B" (Global Value Chain—2025)
correction: Quarters ranged US$5.09-5.75bn, not 5.5-5.7bn. The CY2025 total, now computed from all four releases, is about US$21.2bn, about 6% below Synopsys's US$22.5bn. The conclusion ('broadly consistent') holds. A superseding inference claim was added.
notes: Populations differ: ESD covers reporting companies only and includes PCB/MCM and services. Synopsys's figure is its own estimate citing Meta Tech, Gartner and TechInsights.

original_interpretation: Interpretation: the foundry, not the EDA vendor, is the gatekeeper of design enablement: PDK access (NDA/approval), signoff tool certification, IP listing/scoring, accepted tape-out data.
evidence_found: TSMC: "request approval by TSMC ... a 3-way NDA" (EUROPRACTICE); TSMC IP Alliance: "extension of the TSMC9000 Program"; Samsung: "EDA tools and flow certifications for foundry process technologies"; Intel: "EDA Alliance partners get early access to Intel's process technologies"; TSMC-Online: "secure online ... information transfer for product design, tape-outs"
correction: The foundry-gatekeeper reading is supported for PDK access, tool/flow certification, IP qualification and tape-out intake. 'Not the EDA vendor' overstates: EDA vendors also gate access through time-based tool licences, and they were the export-control chokepoint in the May 2025 BIS letters (CLM-1502, CLM-1504). Gatekeeping is shared.
notes: Several underlying claims (CLM-1473, CLM-1486, CLM-1490, CLM-0457) are still unverified; this checker re-opened their pages and saw consistent text, but only partial page content for TSMC IP Alliance.

original_interpretation: Interpretation: three post-signoff data handoffs: (1) GDSII/OASIS designer to foundry via portal; (2) post-OPC fractured mask-writer data and job decks from foundry/tape-out group to mask shop; (3) a mask order that SEMI P10 standardises.
evidence_found: Siemens: "Tape-out groups and mask makers are facing a tremendous growth in data volumes"; "Efficient, direct conversion of GDSII ...". Photronics: "CyberMask leverages Semi P10 data specifications"; "Front-end functions automated by CyberMask include: Order entry Data fracture Job decking Measure file generation". TSMC-Online: "...information transfer for product design, tape-outs"
correction: Handoffs (1) and (3) are supported. Handoff (2) is not always foundry-to-mask-shop of fractured data: Photronics says its own CyberMask service does data fracture and job decking on customer data, and Siemens says both tape-out groups and mask makers run mask data prep. So the fracture/job-deck step may happen on either side.
notes: SEMI P10 store page did not render content for this checker, so P10's mask-order fields (pellicles, measurement points) were not re-verified.
